76#main: If he said to another, acquire this bill of release for my slave — the slave goes out to freedom even though it did not reach the slave's hand; but if he said give this document to my slave, he cannot retract and the slave does not go out until the document reaches his hand; therefore one who says give this document to my slave should not give it after death: {Rama: And some say if he gave the document to the agent's hand and said give this document to my slave, it is as if he said acquire for him (Tur in the name of Rabbenu Tam, Rosh, Rashba, Ran).}
77#main: One who commanded at death, so-and-so my maidservant — my heirs shall not enslave her — behold she remains a maidservant as she was, and heirs are forbidden to enslave her; and if he said make comfortable for her, they compel the heirs and they do not enslave her except in work she wishes: {Rama: (And heirs cannot sell her to another, whether he said my heirs shall not enslave her or said make comfortable for her) (Tur in the name of R' Meir of Rothenburg).} And if he commanded and said free her, they compel the heirs to free her.
78#main: A deathly ill person who wrote all his property to his slave and recovered — he retracts regarding property but not regarding the slave, for the name free man already went out upon him.
79#main: One who frees his slave transgresses a positive commandment, for you shall serve them forever; and permitted to free for a mitzvah matter, even from their matters — such as if there were not ten in synagogue, behold he frees his slave and completes ten with him; and all similar; and a maidservant whom people treat with abandon — they compel her master to free her so she marry and the stumbling block be removed (language of Rambam chapter 9 of Laws of Slaves halacha 6).
80#main: One who sells his slave to a gentile or ger toshav — he goes out to freedom, for if he flees from the gentile the master cannot enslave him again; and if he did not flee, they fine the owner to redeem him up to ten times his value and write him a bill of release to permit him to an Israelite woman; and this fine is not collected, judged only by expert court; and if the seller died, heirs are not fined to return the slave for freeing (there chapter 8 of Laws of Slaves): {Rama: If he borrowed money on him for a term that if not paid by a set time the slave is his — if he delivered him immediately to a gentile's hand, he goes out to freedom immediately; and if not delivered immediately to a gentile's hand, when the time comes and he does not pay, he goes out to freedom; but if gentiles collected the debt or violence came and he redeemed himself with it, he does not go out to freedom. If sold to the king's slave who regularly take slaves and animals from wherever found and give their value to owners — he goes out to freedom. If sold on condition to return after time, or except his labor, or except mitzvot, or sold to a Sadducee or apostate — doubt whether he goes out to freedom, and we follow leniency for rabbinic prohibition and he does not go out (all in Tur from Gemara); and some say seizure helps — if he seized from his master's property enough for his value to go out to freedom, gentiles do not remove from him (there in the name of Rambam halacha 8).}
81#main: A slave who circumcised and immersed for servitude and cast himself to a gentile and his master cannot extract him, or was captured and they do not wish to give him for redemption — permitted to take their money and can write them a sale document on him.
82#main: One who sells his slave to chutz la'aretz, or Syria, or Acre — he goes out to freedom and they compel the second master to write a bill of release; and he loses the money; and even if he said I do not wish to take him to chutz la'aretz, let him be enslaved in Eretz Yisrael — they do not listen to him: {Rama: (And this law applies even now) (Tur and Beit Yosef in the name of Rambam halacha 9).}
83#main: A slave who went after his master to Syria and sold him there — he lost his right. When do we say this? When the master went intending not to return to Eretz Yisrael; but if the master's intent was to return and the slave went after him and sold him there — the slave goes out to freedom and they compel the buyer to free him (language of Rambam there halacha 8).
84#main: A slave who said he wishes to go up to Eretz Yisrael — they compel his master to go up with him or sell him to one who will bring him there; if the master wished to go to chutz la'aretz, he cannot take his slave out until the slave agrees; and this law applies at all times, even now when the land is in gentile hands.
85#main: A slave who fled from chutz la'aretz to the Land — they do not return him to servitude; concerning him it is said you shall not deliver a slave to his master; and they tell the master to write him a bill of release and write him a debt document for his value until his hand reaches and he pays; and if the master does not wish to free him, beit din uproots his servitude from upon him and he goes his way.
